subtype: Approach: dividing jobs by what each person is good at [Action]
passage: Thursday. Group project day! Our chart is on the water cycle. At first we all wanted to do the same fun bits. Then I said, why don't we give each person the job they like best? Meera loves drawing, so she does the pictures. Aman writes neatly, so he does the sentences. Riya likes cutting and pasting, so she gets the scissors. Karan speaks well, so he will present. I checked facts and helped everyone. Nobody argued even once. We finished before the bell, and Meera's rain clouds look better than anything I could draw. Manjula.

qa.q: Who is going to present the chart?
Why do you think Manjula is pleased at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Manjula is pleased because the jobs matched what people like, nobody argued, and the chart finished before the bell. 😊

qa.q: What alternative approach could the group use if a member falls behind, and why?
qa.a: The group could check in halfway and let others share the slow job. Then the chart would still be ready on time.

qa.q: How might Meera see her job in the group?
qa.a: Meera got to do the drawing she loves, so the pictures probably feel like a real contribution, and the praise for the clouds shows the group values it.

grounding: The group assigns drawing, writing, cutting and presenting by what each member is good at, so the work moves faster with less quarrelling.
